description: Found in defk-hki. flag_strip/3 keeps a strip with joined checks (overflow, bounds) checked when an unchecked a.data[j] uses an index j assigned in the strip (fixed_indices?/3), because a flagged run computes on after a failed check and j could come from a wrong value. That is conservative: j = i + 1 computed only from the loop counter and loop-invariant values is exact in the flagged run too (test: shifted_sum in test/non_finite_test.exs stays :checked). Done when a strip-assigned index whose assignment uses only fixed values (recursively, no flagged helper with a non-fixed operand) is accepted, the memory-safety argument in priv/defk_runtime.h (flat strips) still holds and is updated, and shifted_sum runs flagged with its mixed-error tests passing.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** A flagged strip accepts an unchecked access whose index is assigned in the strip from fixed values only (e.g. j = i + 1), so such strips run flagged instead of checked

**Current behavior:**
Flagged strips (joined overflow/bounds checks, computing on after a failed check) are refused when an unchecked access uses an index assigned inside the strip, because in a flagged run a value could be wrong after a failed check. That is conservative for indices computed only from the loop counter and loop-invariant values: shifted_sum (the non-finite test file) stays :checked although its j = i + 1 is exact in the flagged run too.

**Desired behavior:**
- An index assigned in the strip is accepted when its assignment uses only fixed values: the loop counter, loop invariants, literals, and other strip-assigned values that are themselves fixed (recursively), through operations whose result cannot be affected by a failed check (no flagged helper with a non-fixed operand, no value read from memory).
- Anything else stays refused as today.
- The memory-safety argument for flat/flagged strips in the runtime header is updated to state why a fixed index is safe in a flagged run.

**Key interfaces:**
- The strip classification (flagged vs checked) and its fixed-index test in the compiler; the runtime header's safety comment; the fast-path report's strip notes

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] shifted_sum runs flagged (report and C), and its mixed-error tests (bounds + non-finite + overflow in one strip) pass with the same results as before
- [ ] Negative tests: an index assigned from an array read, from a value that can overflow under the flag, or from a non-fixed helper keeps the strip checked
- [ ] Agreement and forced-yield tests pass; `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Other reasons a strip is checked; relational facts (defk-2mz)

title: Flagged strips: allow an unchecked access whose index is assigned exactly in the strip
